13% of foreign residents in Gyeonggi live in makeshift residences

Gyeonggi Province has seen its foreign resident numbers surge over 14-fold since 2000, but a recent study indicated that a substantial portion of them are living in housing not meant for permanent residence. Of the 680,000 non-citizen residents in Gyeonggi Province as of 2024, 13.3 percent were residing in greenhouses, shipping containers, and dormitories that are not legally defined as homes, according to the Gyeonggi Research Institute. The proportion of migrants living in non-permanent housing was far higher than the 2.2 percent recorded for Koreans that year. In the city of Pocheon, in particular, 42.7 percent of foreign residents were living in non-homes. Often referred to as part of the capital region alongside Incheon and Seoul, Gyeonggi Province is South Korea's most populous region, accounting for roughly a quarter of the entire population. The number of foreign residents in the province has increased exponentially since the 46,000 recorded in 2000. But the researchers found that many are living in structures that are barely habitable. "In some cases, household appliances like the refrigerator and the washing machine were placed inside a greenhouse, where (the resident) was living for an extended period of time," the study noted. Some of the greenhouse dwellings had panels installed to support the structure.
